# Now 2.10.80
- Cleaned up lyrics from NetEase and QQ Music: leading and trailing production credits (composer, lyricist, mixing/mastering, and the "Title - Artist" header) are now trimmed, so the overlay shows the actual song from the first sung line. - Credit trimming only touches the start and end of the lyric and only for those two sources, so real lyrics — and LRCLIB / Apple Music lyrics — are never altered.

# Now 2.10.79
- Added two more synchronized-lyrics sources — NetEase Cloud Music and QQ Music — alongside LRCLIB and the Apple Music local cache. Many songs (especially on YouTube Music) that previously had no timed lyrics should now find them. - Sources are tried in order (LRCLIB → NetEase → QQ Music) and every match is held to the same strict title/artist/duration check, so a broad catalogue search never attaches the wrong song's lyrics. - Only basic track metadata (title, artist) is sent to any source. No audio, cookies, or account data leaves the device. - Results still persist on disk and each source is time-limited and circuit-broken, so adding sources does not reintroduce slow or stalled lookups.

# Now 2.10.78
- Timed lyrics that resolve successfully are now saved on disk, so previously-working songs keep their lyrics across app restarts and updates. A temporary lyrics-service outage can no longer make most songs appear to lose lyrics. - Lyrics lookups now run behind a source abstraction with a per-source time limit and a circuit breaker, so one slow or unreachable lyrics service can't stall every lookup (the earlier ~31-second stall is bounded to a few seconds). - A genuine "this song has no synced lyrics" result is remembered briefly; a network/outage failure is never cached, so it stays retryable. - Groundwork for additional lyrics sources (beyond LRCLIB and the Apple Music local cache) — new providers can now be added without touching the lookup flow.
